subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: What permanent Mattermost interaction-signing contract should replace the current bot-token-derived secret?
rationale: Changing the signing root repairs a security boundary but also changes a documented integration contract and may require new SecretRef, generated credential, doctor, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Per-account stored secret
options.body: Generate or configure a per-account interaction secret, persist it through the plugin-owned credential path, update docs, and reject old bot-token-derived forgeries after an explicit upgrade path.

options.title: Config-only explicit secret
options.body: Require operators to set a new per-account interaction secret and fail closed when it is missing, accepting a sharper setup and upgrade burden.

options.title: Defer pending broader channel auth review
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers decide whether Mattermost interactions need a shared channel callback-auth design instead of a Mattermost-only contract.

recommendation.title: Per-account stored secret
recommendation.body: Generate or configure a per-account interaction secret, persist it through the plugin-owned credential path, update docs, and reject old bot-token-derived forgeries after an explicit upgrade path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a security-boundary and channel authorization policy choice, and recent history ties steipete to shared channel security hardening.
